northern_ireland.note: Northern Ireland is deliberately out of scope for the DNO section. It does not appear in the Energy Networks Association distribution licence area table, and regulation 3 of SI 2026/848 does not extend to Northern Ireland. Regulations 1 and 2 of that instrument do.

headline_finding: The 28-day notification deadline is not set by individual network operators. It is a national requirement in EREC G98 section 1.1, made under regulation 22(2)(c) of the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 and the Health and Safety Executive's certificate of exemption of August 2008. EREC G98 places the duty to notify on the installer. SI 2026/848, which makes plug-in solar lawful from 27 August 2026, does not mention EREC G98, DNO notification, or any connection procedure. UK Power Networks, the largest operator by licence area, states on both its installer portal and its consumer guidance that only installers can notify it on behalf of customers. Five of the six operators are consistent with the national 28 days; SP Energy Networks publishes 30 days for its commissioning confirmation form and separately asks for notice before or at commissioning. This is a factual record of what each source states, not legal advice.
headline_finding_note: This field reports what primary sources say. It deliberately draws no conclusion about what a householder installing a plug-in device without an installer is required to do; see national_rule.applies_to_diy_householder, which is null.
deadline_uniformity: uniform at 28 days nationally, with SP Energy Networks publishing 30 days for its commissioning confirmation form

route_open_to_householder_summary.note: false is recorded only where the operator states it on its own pages. Everything else is null because the operator does not address the question.

national_rule.quote: the Installer is required to ensure that the DNO is made aware of the Micro-generator installation before the time of commissioning or no later than 28 days (inclusive of the day of commissioning) after commissioning
national_rule.source_document: ENA Engineering Recommendation G98, section 1.1 (restated at 8.3.1)
national_rule.legal_basis: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 Regulation 22(2)(c), and the Certificate of Exemption granted by the Health and Safety Executive in August 2008
national_rule.duty_holder_quote: Your installer must notify the DNO within 28 days of commissioning the generating unit, and provide them with information on the installation. This is a legal requirement.
national_rule.duty_holder_source: ENA Distributed Generation Connection Guide: G98 for Single Premises
national_rule.form: G98 Form B, the Installation Document at Appendix 3 of EREC G98
national_rule.applies_to_diy_householder_note: EREC G98 places the duty on the installer. No primary source consulted states what a householder who installs a plug-in device without an installer must do. This is recorded as unresolved rather than guessed.
national_rule.not_referenced_by_si_2026_848_note: The full text of SI 2026/848 was read on 2026-08-01. It amends product safety requirements and does not mention EREC G98, DNO notification, or any connection procedure. The notification framework is separate from the legalisation.
